data.narrative:
Path Robotics, a Series D robotics and manufacturing company founded by Andy and Alex Lonsberry, has raised $271M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private peers and one public comparable, spanning robotics and advanced manufacturing at Series C through Series E stages.

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression analysis uses the $271M total raised as a baseline proxy and applies a 1.5x multiplier typical for Series D to next-stage advancement, yielding $406M. Peer-median analysis across five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Divergent ($2.3B, Series E), Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Hadrian ($1.6B, Series D), Agile Robots ($1.0B, Series C), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B, Series C)—produces a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.3B.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $346M (low) to $1.8B (high), with a median of $1.0B. The substantial spread reflects uncertainty regarding Path's relative positioning within the peer set: stage-progression anchors to capital deployed, while peer-median reflects market pricing of comparable-stage competitors. Key variables affecting ultimate valuation include Path's revenue trajectory relative to peers and whether capital efficiency metrics align with higher-valued Series D comparables like Exotec or Hadrian.
